description: HPO terms for the 20 lad1 checklist items (configs/checklists/lad1.json), chosen on 2026-10-20 by a Claude helper from the pinned HPO release by name and synonym search and hierarchy checks (pipeline/extract/hpo_lookup.py), D-40. 'observed' is the one term a phenopacket may assert when the item is observed; null where the item is a composite, or where HPO has no term matching the item's scope (the free-text feature rows carry the specific term). 'excluded' lists every term a phenopacket may mark excluded when the item is explicitly absent. Flagged for review by Jimmy or the panel; not a pre-registered choice.

delayed umbilical cord separation.note: Delayed umbilical cord separation (exact name match).

omphalitis.note: Neonatal omphalitis, whose EXACT synonyms include 'Omphalitis' and 'Umbilical cord stump infection'.

leukocytosis or neutrophilia.note: Increased total leukocyte count (EXACT 'Leukocytosis') and Increased total neutrophil count (EXACT 'Neutrophilia'); neither is an ancestor of the other, so the composite has no single observed term.

absence of pus formation.note: Decreased inflammatory response: HPO has no term for absent pus (searched pus, purulent, suppuration, exudate, neutrophil migration), and this is the nearest clinical term, though broader than the item; review whether to keep it or leave the item unbound. Pus being present is not an HPO abnormality, so nothing is excluded.

skin or soft tissue infections.note: No single HPO term covers skin and soft tissue infection; excluded are Cellulitis (EXACT 'Skin infection'), Unusual skin infection (covers recurrent bacterial skin infections and pyoderma), Cutaneous abscess, Subcutaneous abscess and Unusual fascia infection (EXACT 'Unusual soft tissue necrotizing infection'), none of which is an ancestor of another.

necrotic skin ulcers or pyoderma gangren.note: Pyoderma gangrenosum (child of Skin ulcer). Skin ulcer itself is broader than the item (it includes pressure and other non-necrotic ulcers), so it is neither asserted nor excluded; HPO has no 'necrotic skin ulcer' term.

impaired wound healing.note: Poor wound healing; HPO has no separate 'impaired wound healing' term.

periodontitis or gingivitis.note: Periodontitis and Gingivitis; neither is an ancestor of the other and their shared parent (Abnormal gingiva morphology) is broader than the item.

tooth loss.note: Spontaneous tooth loss (EXACT 'Loss of teeth', 'Premature loss of teeth'); its children cover primary and permanent teeth.

lower respiratory tract infection.note: HPO's only plain-scope grouping is 'Unusual lower respiratory tract infection', which is narrower in wording and also has Acute respiratory distress syndrome as a child, so it is not used; excluded are its infectious children Pneumonia, Bronchitis and Unusual bronchiolitis, plus Lung abscess and Recurrent lower respiratory tract infections.

otitis media.note: Otitis media (exact name match; EXACT 'Middle ear infection').

sepsis.note: Sepsis (exact name match); neonatal, bacterial and fungal sepsis are descendants.

meningitis.note: Meningitis (exact name match); bacterial, viral and fungal meningitis are descendants.

gastrointestinal infections.note: HPO has no plain 'gastrointestinal infection' term; 'Unusual gastrointestinal infection' also holds cholecystitis, splenic abscess and liver infections, so only its gut-infection children are excluded: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract, Unusual infectious gastroenteritis, Unusual infectious colitis, Clostridium difficile enteritis and colitis.

colitis or gastrointestinal inflammatory.note: Gastrointestinal inflammation (EXACT 'GI inflammation'); Colitis is a descendant (via Inflammation of the large intestine), so one term covers both parts.

fungal infections.note: HPO groups fungal infections under 'Unusual fungal infection' (which contains candidiasis, invasive and recurrent fungal infections), narrower in wording than the item, so observed is null; Fungemia, Chronic monilial nail infection and Fungal hair infection sit outside it and are excluded as well.

bcg vaccine complications.note: BCG-associated disease (EXACT 'Adverse reaction to BCG vaccination', 'BCG vaccine adverse event'); BCGitis and BCGosis are descendants.
